about: SmartAssist's voice commands on Android. Each command has patterns: the words people say, with {placeholders} for the parts that change. Patterns are tried from top to bottom and the first one that fits wins, so put longer patterns before shorter ones. Write patterns in lower case, without punctuation. Each command's examples must match one of its patterns (src/__tests__/voiceCommands.test.ts checks this). Replies are what SmartAssist says; keep their {placeholders}. Rebuild the app (npx expo run:android) after a change.

patterns: send a message to {contact} on {messenger} saying {message}
examples: Send a message to Mum saying I'm on my way
send a WhatsApp message to Tunde saying call me later
tell Aunty Ngozi that the meeting is at five
text David saying I am home

patterns: how much battery do i have
examples: How much battery do I have?

replies.notHeard: I didn't hear anything. Tap Speak and try again.
replies.notUnderstood: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Try saying: open WhatsApp.
replies.needMicrophone: SmartAssist needs the microphone to hear you. Tap Speak again and allow it.
replies.needContacts: SmartAssist needs your contacts to find {contact}.
replies.needPhone: SmartAssist needs permission to make calls.
replies.needSms: SmartAssist needs permission to send text messages.
replies.noApp: I couldn't find an app called {app}.
replies.noContact: I couldn't find {contact} in your contacts.
replies.confirmMessage: Send: {message}. To {contact}, on {messenger}? Say yes or no.
replies.pressSend: I've typed your message to {contact}. Press Send to send it.
replies.unsupportedMessenger: I can send messages on WhatsApp or by text. I can't send on {messenger} yet.
replies.help: You can say: open WhatsApp. Send a message to Mum saying I'm on my way. Call Mum. What time is it. Read the screen.
